newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah weaker on minister's comments.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah weaker on minister's comments.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah weakened against the dollar in slow early Monday trading following overnight comments by Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad on the rupiah's depreciation target, dealers said.
They said spot rupiah edged down to 2,321.75/22.25 at 0230 GMT from 2,319.25/20.00 at the opening. It fell to a low of 2,324.5 in early Singapore trading.
One currency analyst in Singapore said the overnight statement by Mar'ie triggered off some dollar buying.
Mar'ie said in Washington that Indonesia would rather have its rupiah undervalued than overvalued.
The minister said the country intended to depreciate the currency by five percent per year against the U.S. dollar.
"The market was very short of dollars. The comment gave reason to cover," the analyst said, adding that the rupiah has only being minimally depreciated so far.
He said the statement might indicate a possible faster depreciation of the rupiah to meet the government target.
However, the analyst said the minister had to make that kind of comment because otherwise the yield offered by the rupiah would be relatively higher and induce more capital inflows.
Dealers said in Jakarta said the dollar uptrend was not firmly supported as further appreciation was capped on its attractive yield and market concerns on liquidity.
They said operators' main worry this morning was liquidity supply in the money market because of the month-end factor.
The worry was indicated by a light uptrend in overnight swap which inched up to 0.7 points from 0.6.
Tom/next swap rate was relatively expensive at 0.65/0.75.
Dealers said longer-term swap rates were little changed and volume was thin in early trading.
One-month swap was last at 16.75/17.75, two at 32.00/34.0, three at 48.00/50.00 and six at 96.00/99.00 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,315/2,507 and the conversion rate also by one point to 2,315/2,363 on Friday.
